definition: If you are taken aback by something, you are completely surprised or shocked by it.
sentence: I was taken aback by his sudden resignation from the company.

definition: An abacus is a simple device for calculating, consisting of a frame with rows of wires or grooves along which beads are slid.
sentence: The child learned to perform basic math using a wooden abacus.

definition: If you abandon a place, thing, or person, you leave them permanently or stop looking after them.
sentence: The crew had to abandon the sinking ship before the storm hit.

definition: If something bad or undesirable abates, it becomes much less strong or severe.
sentence: We waited for the heavy wind to abate before continuing our hike.

definition: Your ability to do something is the fact that you can do it, usually because you have the necessary skills or talent.
sentence: She demonstrated a remarkable ability to learn new languages quickly.

definition: If you are able to do something, you have the physical or mental power to do it.
sentence: With enough practice, he will be able to run a marathon.

definition: If something is abnormal, it is completely different from what is usual or expected, usually in a worrying way.
sentence: The warm weather was highly abnormal for this time of year.

definition: If you are aboard a ship, aircraft, or train, you are on it or in it.
sentence: The flight attendant welcomed the passengers aboard the aircraft.

definition: If you are talking or thinking about a subject, you are considering that subject.
sentence: We spent the evening talking about our plans for the upcoming summer.

definition: If one thing is above another, it is situated at a higher level than the other thing.
sentence: The eagle soared high above the snow-capped mountain peaks.
